overview: IAG is the largest general insurance company in Australia and New Zealand, selling personal and commercial insurance through a portfolio of trusted brands including NRMA Insurance, CGU, WFI, SGIO, SGIC, ROLLiN', State, AMI, NZI and Lumley, and (since September 2025) RACQ Insurance. The Group operates through three segments -- Retail Insurance Australia (direct personal and some commercial lines), Intermediated Insurance Australia (broker-distributed commercial and personal lines) and New Zealand (direct and broker-distributed) -- and has largely exited its former Asian operations to focus on its two home markets. IAG has historically ceded a fixed ~32.5% quota share of its whole-of-account premiums and claims to a panel of global reinsurers including a 20% share to Berkshire Hathaway's National Indemnity, smoothing earnings volatility in exchange for a share of underwriting profit.

business_model.summary: IAG earns gross written premium (GWP) across personal lines (motor, home), commercial lines (SME, workers' compensation, professional risks) and compulsory third-party (CTP) motor schemes, cedes roughly a third of premium (and claims) to quota-share and catastrophe reinsurers, and retains an underwriting margin plus investment income earned on technical reserves and shareholders' funds. FY26 reported GWP was $18,412m (+7.6% YoY), insurance profit $1,552m (14.7% reported margin, 15.0% underlying margin) and net profit after tax $1,022m. Revenue is largely annually renewing/recurring (policy renewals), not project-based, though volumes and pricing are cyclical with claims inflation, natural catastrophe activity and reinsurance costs.

revenue_streams.name: Retail Insurance Australia (motor, home, CTP, direct SME) - NRMA/RACV/RACQ/ROLLiN'
revenue_streams.trend: growing (RACQI acquisition, mid single-digit underlying growth)

revenue_streams.name: Intermediated Insurance Australia (commercial short/long-tail, personal lines via brokers) - CGU/WFI
New Zealand (direct and broker) - State/AMI/NZI/Lumley
revenue_streams.trend: flat to declining in AUD terms (NZD weakness, competitive broker market)

business_model.customer_type: Mass-market B2C (personal motor/home) plus B2B SME and corporate commercial lines and government CTP schemes
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia ~81% of Group insurance revenue (Retail 56% + Intermediated 25%), New Zealand ~19%; Asia operations largely divested in prior years

competitive_position.market_position: Largest general insurer in Australia and New Zealand by GWP, with leading market share in personal motor/home insurance and a leading position in rural/regional intermediated commercial lines via CGU and WFI

moat_factors.description: Owns/distributes NRMA, RACV (JV), RACQ, CGU, WFI, ROLLiN', State, AMI, NZI and Lumley, giving broad reach across direct, club/loyalty, bank-partner and broker channels that would be very costly for a new entrant to replicate

160-year heritage brands with high customer trust; disaster response capability (Major Event Command Centre, mobile claims fleet, 150+ dedicated catastrophe claims staff) supports retention after major weather events

Long-dated whole-of-account quota share (32.5%, including 20% with Berkshire Hathaway's National Indemnity to 2029) and multi-year catastrophe covers smooth earnings and provide access to capital markets, but this is available in principle to large peers too and is a capital-efficiency tool rather than a hard moat

Ongoing multi-year platform transformation (Guidewire Cloud, 8m+ retail policies migrated) and growing AI/agentic deployment (90+ AI agents, 60%+ staff usage) aimed at underwriting/claims efficiency and fraud detection
APRA general insurance licensing, capital and prudential requirements are a barrier to new entrants, though they also constrain IAG's own capital flexibility

weaknesses: High geographic/customer concentration in Australia and NZ leaves no diversification benefit outside two closely correlated, catastrophe-exposed markets
Heavy reliance on quota-share reinsurance means a meaningful share of underwriting profit accrues to reinsurance partners rather than shareholders
M&A execution risk evident in RACQI integration (natural perils losses on the acquired book before it was folded into Group reinsurance drove FY26 margin miss)

ACCC blocked the ~A$1.35bn RAC Insurance (WA) acquisition on 23 September 2026 on competition grounds, casting doubt on IAG's ability to replicate the RACQ playbook in WA and highlighting regulatory limits on further market consolidation

growth_drivers: RACQ Insurance integration (completed 1 September 2025) adding ~1.7m Queensland members and driving FY26 GWP growth; further synergies and full-year contribution expected in FY27
Ambition 2030 target of growing from ~9.5m to 11m+ customers and over $25bn in GWP, underpinned by cross-sell across the multi-brand portfolio
Technology/AI-led efficiency: cloud platform migration (8m+ retail policies), 90+ deployed AI agents in claims/fraud/service, targeting lower expense ratios and faster claims cycle times
Structural premium growth from rate increases covering claims inflation, rising asset values, underinsurance awareness and population growth in Australia/NZ
Potential (contested) further Western Australia expansion via RAC Insurance, subject to a Public Benefit Application after the ACCC's Phase 2 opposition
Capital management: ongoing buybacks ($200m completed FY26) and dividend growth (32.0cps FY26, up from 31.0cps FY25) as capital normalises post-RACQI

business.description: FY26 net natural perils costs of $1,579m were $114m above the $1,465m allowance, driven by severe weather hitting the newly acquired RACQI book before it was folded into Group reinsurance on 1 January 2026; 65 weather events in Australia and 44 in NZ in FY26 alone

RACQI's natural perils losses in 1H26 (a $174m loss on the acquired portfolio) show integration/reinsurance-timing risk; further large-scale M&A (e.g. RAC Insurance) faces both integration and regulatory execution risk
Commercial strata premium down ~20%, IIA personal lines and NZ broker channel (NZI) GWP declining amid 'fiercely competitive' markets and underwriting discipline trade-offs

Rising premiums to cover claims inflation and reinsurance costs are drawing political and regulatory scrutiny (Small Business Insurance Inquiry, NZ Treasury affordability review) that could constrain future rate increases

financial.description: CET1 multiple fell to 1.14x PCA at 30 June 2026 (FY25: 1.47x) and total PCA multiple to 2.12x (FY25: 2.43x), reflecting RACQI acquisition funding and buybacks/dividends, though still within/near target ranges (CET1 target 0.9-1.1x, total capital target 1.6-1.8x)
NZ GWP is ~19% of Group revenue; NZD weakness reduced reported (AUD) NZ GWP by 8.0% in FY26 even though local-currency GWP fell only 2.7%, and also reduced the FX translation reserve by $189m
Technical reserve investment yield fell to 4.8% in FY26 from 5.3% in FY25; shareholders' funds carry ~28% growth-asset allocation (equities/alternatives), exposing earnings to market movements

Reinsurance expense grew to $7,449m combined (quota-share + non-quota-share) roughly in line with premium growth in FY26, but availability/pricing of global catastrophe reinsurance capacity is a structural cost risk in an increasingly loss-heavy environment

regulatory.description: On 23 September 2026 the ACCC opposed IAG's ~A$1.35bn acquisition of RAC Insurance on competition grounds (would have given IAG ~55-65% WA motor and ~50-60% WA home insurance share); IAG must now pursue a Public Benefit Application for any path forward, with outcome and timing uncertain

APRA expects independent non-executive directors on regulated subsidiary boards (driving new appointments to RACQI board); ongoing prudential capital standards constrain capital flexibility and M&A funding choices

IAG released the bulk of its COVID-19 BI provision (~A$200m of an A$380m provision) after Federal Court test-case rulings and the BI class action ceasing to be a class action in March 2025, but a residual provision remains for potential further valid claims
FY26 is IAG's first mandatory Sustainability Report under AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures, adding compliance cost and disclosure/litigation risk around climate transition claims

macro.description: Home inflation ~10% in FY26 driven by large water/fire claims; motor inflation mid-single-digit; building/parts/labour cost inflation continues to pressure claims costs ahead of premium repricing

IAG's own research (Severe Weather in a Changing Climate, IAG Resilient Futures Report) and rising natural peril allowances ($1,465m FY27 vs $1,283m FY25) reflect a structurally rising cost base from more frequent/severe weather events

General insurance is largely non-discretionary (compulsory motor/CTP, mortgage-linked home cover) which limits volume cyclicality, but affordability pressure can drive underinsurance or policy lapses in a downturn

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian and NZ general insurance markets are growing on rate (claims inflation, reinsurance cost pass-through) and modestly on volume (population, asset values, underinsurance awareness); industry consolidation is being actively contested by regulators (ACCC blocking of RAC Insurance deal)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - GWP and volumes are relatively defensive (compulsory/mortgage-linked lines) but underwriting margins and reported profit are highly cyclical with natural catastrophe experience, reserve releases and investment markets
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - technical reserve investment income (duration ~2 years) and discount rate movements on claims liabilities directly affect reported profit; falling yields were a FY26 headwind (4.8% vs 5.3% technical reserve yield)
key_input_costs: Building materials and construction/motor repair costs (claims inflation)
Labour costs for claims handling and supply chain partners

recent_developments.event: ACCC formally opposed IAG's proposed ~A$1.35bn acquisition of RAC Insurance (WA), finding it would substantially lessen competition (55-65% WA motor share, 50-60% WA home share); IAG to pursue a Public Benefit Application to seek a path forward

FY26 full-year results: NPAT $1,022m (down 24.8% YoY) on GWP $18,412m (+7.6%), reported insurance margin 14.7% (underlying 15.0%), full-year dividend 32.0cps (up from 31.0cps), $200m on-market buyback completed
FY27 guidance issued: GWP growth 5-8%, reported insurance margin 14.5-16.5%, assuming a $1,491m natural perils allowance and no material reserve releases/macro movements

Phillip Gibson appointed Chief Executive of IAG New Zealand (ex-Accenture/Aviva Canada/Allstate/Travelers); former NZ CEO Amanda Whiting moved to newly created Chief Strategy and Transformation Officer role

Completed acquisition of 90% of RACQ Insurance Limited (RACQI) in Queensland, welcoming ~840 new employees and ~1.7m RACQ members; RACQI experienced severe natural perils losses in its first four months before being integrated into Group reinsurance from 1 January 2026

FY26 interim results: 1H26 NPAT $505m (down 35.1% YoY), reported insurance margin 13.5% (underlying 15.1%), impacted by $174m loss on the not-yet-reinsured RACQI portfolio amid severe hail/storm events
Group launched 'Ambition 2030' refreshed strategy targeting 11m+ customers, $25bn+ premiums, ROE of 15%+, high-single-digit EPS growth and top-quartile TSR

items.vs_prior: new guidance issued with FY26 results
items.notes: Reflects rate increases covering claims inflation plus direct customer/volume growth; includes mid-single-digit underlying growth in AU/NZ retail, low-single-digit in AU/NZ intermediated, plus ~$300m of additional RACQI premium (2 extra months) and ~$100m multi-year workers' comp premium, partly offset by ~$150m Honey portfolio exit

items.vs_prior: new guidance; compares to FY26 actual of 14.7%
items.notes: Assumes FY27 natural perils allowance of $1,491m (in line with long-term perils volatility cover attachment point), no material prior period reserve releases/strengthening, and no material FX or investment market movements
Stated alongside high-single-digit EPS growth and top-quartile TSR ambitions; FY26 actual ROE was 13.8% (1H26 annualised, cash ROE lower across the year given perils drag)
Some Ambition 2030 targets assume completion of the RAC Insurance (WA) acquisition, which the ACCC has since opposed (23 September 2026), creating risk to this target
FY26 actual GWP was $18,412m; implies continued mid-to-high single digit annual growth through the decade

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Nick Hawkins said FY26 results reflected 'successful pursuit of our strategy' despite a natural perils-driven profit decline, citing completion of the RACQ Insurance acquisition, continued technology platform transformation and the launch of Ambition 2030. Management noted the FY27 margin guidance assumes no repeat of adverse reserve or perils surprises and flagged FX and investment markets as swing factors outside its control. Following the ACCC's 23 September 2026 opposition to the RAC Insurance (WA) deal, IAG stated it will lodge a Public Benefit Application, introducing uncertainty around the WA growth leg of its Ambition 2030 plan.

bull_case: Largest, most diversified AU/NZ general insurer with multi-brand distribution scale that is very difficult and slow for competitors to replicate
RACQ Insurance integration (now fully in Group reinsurance from January 2026) should normalize margins in FY27 and add a full year of contribution after a perils-heavy first year
FY27 guidance (5-8% GWP growth, 14.5-16.5% margin) implies margin recovery from the FY26 trough, supported by rate increases still catching up to claims inflation

Consistent capital returns -- 32.0cps FY26 dividend (up YoY), $200m buyback completed, dividend policy of 60-80% of NPAT payout -- with capital ratios still within/near target bands despite the RACQI-driven dip
Technology/AI investment (cloud platform, 90+ AI agents) offers a credible path to structurally lower expense ratios over the Ambition 2030 horizon
bear_case: ACCC has blocked the RAC Insurance (WA) acquisition on competition grounds, casting doubt on IAG's ability to keep consolidating the AU/NZ market and putting a key leg of the Ambition 2030 customer/GWP targets at risk

Reported earnings are highly volatile and were down sharply in FY26 (NPAT -24.8%) on worse-than-allowed natural perils experience; climate change appears to be structurally raising the peril allowance and cost base each year
CET1 and total capital multiples have declined meaningfully post-RACQI (CET1 1.14x vs 1.47x FY25), narrowing headroom for further buybacks or M&A without fresh capital

Quota-share reinsurance cedes a large, fixed share of underwriting economics (32.5%, including 20% to Berkshire Hathaway) to reinsurance partners, capping the upside IAG shareholders capture even in strong underwriting years
Regulatory/political scrutiny of insurance affordability (parliamentary inquiries, NZ Treasury reviews) could constrain IAG's ability to keep repricing for claims and reinsurance cost inflation
